s0: Meet Site Memory: a private, always-on memory for a one-person installer. You fit cameras, alarms and boilers across hundreds of homes, and you forget which recorder is in which loft. And your apprentice doesn't know how you do the job at all.
s1: After a job, type a note like a text to yourself. The key safe code is spotted on the device and sealed into an encrypted vault before anything leaves. Nemotron 3 Nano, on Nebius Token Factory, sorts the rest into kit, access and dates. Nothing is saved until you approve it.
s2: Next visit, pull up outside and ask what you need to know. In a few seconds Nemotron writes a thirty-second brief. Every line cites the note it came from, and lines it can't back up are dropped. The code stays in the vault, revealed only on the device.
s3: Every evening at half eight, the nightly pass runs by itself on the bigger Nemotron 3 Super. It reads tomorrow's jobs, each property's kit and the attached skills, and writes a prep list for every stop, plus what's falling due this month.
s4: Site Memory also learns how you work. Apprentice Skills are checklists Nemotron writes from your notes and your edits, versioned with diffs. Export one as a plain checklist for an apprentice or a sub. Codes are never printed.
s5: Ask for the next version, and Nemotron 3 Super proposes changes grounded in notes it hasn't learned from yet. Nothing changes until you approve, edit, park or leave it, and every decision is journalled.
s6: Every AI call runs live on Nebius Token Factory with NVIDIA Nemotron 3: Nano at the door, Super for the nightly pass and skills. Here's the last call, with its latency and tokens.
s7: Site Memory. A memory for every property, and an apprentice that writes down how you do the job. Built by MN Labs.
